reviewer: Independent Astra Max source and anatomical registration reviewer
scope: Four exact native Union A east and Confederate A west contact/casualty sheets; source authoring acceptance only. Integration, playback and exact installation acceptance remain separate.
referenceMethod: Each army has four manually selected crown-only and support-sole-only ROIs. Recompute alpha>=64 capTop and exclusive soleGroundY; bodySpan=soleGroundY-capTop. Use the half-up rounded median contact span, shared unchanged with that army's casualty sheet. Projected crouch/fall height changes are intentional.
rootMethod: Select native integer X from projected pelvis/torso anatomy, independently of the ground ROI X. Select Y as the exclusive maximum alpha>=64 row in the specified boot, knee, palm/knuckle or prone trouser support ROI. Do not use the whole silhouette or weapon bounds. Semantic placement is a model-assisted visual judgment, not a physical skeleton certification.
rootPlacementUncertaintyNativePixels: Approximately 6-10 pixels for anatomical projection; exact ROI extrema are reproducible but the semantic support choice remains a visual judgment.

pairScaleAssessment.union: No material enlarged or shrunken casualty partner was found. The tilted stumble cap/roll and compressed fall projections vary modestly; boots, limbs and kit remain coherent with the contact sheet. Union roll shading is warmer than the grayer v5 reference, while placement and equipment remain consistent.
pairScaleAssessment.confederate: The casualty first cap/roll is modestly smaller in projection than the low contact guard. Other postures and body/boot proportions remain coherent; no whole-pair scale blocker was found. The shared 405-pixel contact reference is retained without phase normalization.
pairScaleAssessment.interpretation: These are bounded source judgments. Source-to-game transitions and exact production playback still require the separate final integration review.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis centre X; nearer left-of-image rear boot sole lower edge for Y, separate from the forward rifle.
Projected pelvis centre X in the short east extension; nearer left-of-image rear boot sole lower edge for Y.
Projected pelvis centre X in recovery; nearer left-of-image rear boot sole lower edge for Y.
Projected pelvis centre X in the high guard; nearer left-of-image rear boot sole lower edge for Y.

cells.observation: East-facing low guard retains navy cap/coat, blue trousers, straps, roll and canteen. Two separated grips and both boot supports are legible; the rifle clears the cell.
Eastward extension uses a widened stance and a straight bayonet below shoulder level. Both hands remain distinguishable; the pose differs from the v5 cheek-fired aim.
East-facing low recovery lowers the point and returns the hands toward the trunk. Head, roll, boots and limb proportions remain coherent with the first two cells.
East-facing compact high guard lifts the rifle diagonally while the stock stays low. Separate hands and feet remain readable; the raised point is a guard, not a new body bearing.

alphaDiagnostics.brightRedMethod: R>180, G<90, B<100 and alpha>=64; a descriptive pixel count, not a cleanup or anatomy gate.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis centre X; nearer left-of-image boot sole lower edge for Y in the backward stumble.
Projected pelvis centre X; lowered left-of-image blue knee cloth underside for Y, excluding the trailing boot and forward sole.
Projected pelvis/torso X; bracing right-of-image palm underside for Y in the collapse, isolated below the rifle.
Projected pelvis centre X; grounded near-knee blue trouser underside for Y at prone rest. The ROI lies left of the rifle stock and excludes the boots.

cells.observation: East-facing backward stumble tilts the head and raises the held rifle. Cap/roll projection is slightly smaller than the contact guard, but the boots, limbs and kit remain coherent as a pair.
East-facing knee drop preserves the same cap, coat and equipment. Lowered knee and forward boot are distinguishable; natural height loss is not treated as a scale error.
East-facing supported collapse extends the leg and places one palm below the rifle. The other hand retains its grip; head/roll projection changes with the lowered torso.
East-facing side/prone rest keeps the same kit and a relaxed rifle alongside the body. Folded legs and near forearm remain readable; the selected trouser support excludes the stock.

cells.observation: West-facing low guard retains gray cap/coat, cream trousers, pack/roll and tan canteen. Two grips, separate legs and a straight rifle are visible with clear margins.
Westward extension has a braced stance and a rifle below shoulder level. The forward hand is clear; the rear hand and stock are partly occluded by the near forearm, limiting fine grip judgment.
West-facing low recovery draws the stock toward the waist and drops the point. Both hand positions and separate supports are legible; kit and proportions remain consistent.
West-facing high guard lifts the bayonet while keeping the stock below the chest. The hands remain separate and the body keeps its west bearing; raised weapon direction is a parry.

alphaDiagnostics.brightRedMethod: R>180, G<90, B<100 and alpha>=64; a descriptive pixel count, not a cleanup or anatomy gate.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis centre X; nearer right-of-image rear boot sole lower edge for Y during the loss of balance.
Projected pelvis centre X; lowered right-of-image knee cloth underside for Y, excluding the trailing boot and rifle.
Projected pelvis/torso X; near hand knuckle underside below the rifle grip for Y while collapsing. The ROI excludes the stock tip and trailing boots.
Projected pelvis centre X; near upper-leg cream cloth underside for Y at prone rest, to the right of the rifle stock and away from the boots.

cells.observation: West-facing loss of balance gathers the legs and leans the torso back. Cap/roll are modestly smaller in projection than contact guard; the body/boot proportions remain coherent without an oversized partner.
West-facing supported knee drop retains the gray/cream kit and lowers the torso. The bent knee, front sole and trailing boot remain distinguishable.
West-facing collapse lowers both hands with the rifle and extends a leg behind. The near knuckle underside supplies a bounded support cue; exact weight distribution is not certified.
West-facing prone rest retains the same equipment and leg proportions. The near upper-leg cloth provides a support cue clear of the rifle; fine ground pressure and anatomy remain uncertified.

alphaDiagnostics.brightRedMethod: R>180, G<90, B<100 and alpha>=64; a descriptive pixel count, not a cleanup or anatomy gate.

limitations: Confederate contact cell 1 partly occludes the rear hand and stock. Its below-shoulder extension differs from reference firing, but exact two-hand mechanics and historical drill are not certified.
Low-alpha colored fringes/noise remain, including near some native cell edges. Solid-alpha margins pass; fringe-free edges are not certified.
Per-pose head/roll projection and shading are not perfectly identical. Pair scale is accepted by bounded visual comparison, not by substituting a stationary-body span threshold.
Prone and collapsing supports are inferred from visible boots, knees, hands or cloth contact cues. Exact ground pressure, skeletal anatomy and real physical weight transfer are not certified.
This acceptance does not establish playback quality, GPU behavior, human usability, final installation approval, default promotion or complete infantry-family coverage.
